newsitem.title: USA: ITT unveils massive plan to thwart Hilton bid.
newsitem.headline: ITT unveils massive plan to thwart Hilton bid.

text.p: Hotel and casino giant ITT Corp. launched a massive restructuring on Wednesday to thwart a $6.5 billion hostile bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp. by breaking into three companies and buying back $2.1 billion in stock.
Under the long-awaited plan that received widespread praise on Wall Street, ITT plans to create a new company called ITT Destinations Inc. for its prized casino and hotel business.

The proposal also calls for the formation of a new ITT Corp. for its highly profitable world telephone directories operations, and the company's educational services unit will be contained in ITT Educational Services Inc.

"Separating our lodging and gaming operations from ITT's other remaining assets is in keeping with our goal of creating current value for ITT shareholders while enhancing the long-term prospects and strategic opportunities for each business," said ITT Chairman Rand Araskog, who will hold the position of chairman and chief executive officer of ITT Destinations.
The move comes about two years after a spin-off that split the wide-ranging conglomerate into the current ITT, as well as two other companies for its industrial and insurance operations.
The current ITT Corp.'s core hotel and casino business includes the Sheraton and Caesars brands.

ITT also said it would spend $2.1 billion to repurchase 30 million of its common shares at $70 each, or about 26 percent of its outstanding shares. The company said it plans to buy back the entire $2.0 billion of existing ITT debt through a tender offer later in the year.

Beverly Hills, Calif.-Hilton, which launched its $55 per share hostile offer for ITT in January, immediately blasted the plan. In a press release, the company called the ITT plan a "smoke-and-mirrors scheme" that would be "value destructive" and said a combination of ITT with Hilton would create greater value.
"We will absolutely pursue the legal options that are available to us," said Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman.
Analysts immediately speculated that Hilton may attempt to take over the new Destinations business.

ITT has repeatedly rejected the Hilton bid, calling it financially inadequate. In recent months, ITT has sold non-core assets and amassed a cash pile that was widely expected to be used for a stock buyback or special dividend.
In an interview, Araskog shrugged off Hilton's vows to fight the plan.
"What Hilton does, Hilton does. They've got a business to run. They've got a thing to do. We've got a business to run. We've got a thing to do. They can go do whatever they want to do," he said.
ITT's stock jumped $4.375 to $67 per share, while Hilton rose 12.5 cents to $29.3125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts and investors said the plan was a creative and aggressive structure taken by a company that at one time had been considered lethargic and plodding.
"I think the shareholders are loving this. It's very creative in the laundry list of anti-takeover moves," said Arthur Adler, a partner in the lodging and gaming advisory group at Coopers & Lybrand.

In praising the plan, analysts cited the decision to split into three pieces -- a move that ITT estimates will save $500 million in taxes. They also noted ITT's proposal to create a staggered board for the Destinations hotel and casino business, which would hinder any bid launched by Hilton.

Under the plan, ITT stockholders will keep a their ITT shares, which will represent ownership in the telephone directories business. For each share they hold, they will receive one new share in the hotel and casino company and about 0.25 share of ITT Educational Services.

The company also reported sharply higher earnings for the second quarter of $199 million, or $1.69 a share, on revenues of $1.72 billion, vs. year-earlier earnings of $96 million, or 81 cents a share, on revenues of $1.69 billion.
ITT also said it would scale back its capital expenditure plan in Las Vegas.
In a show of expression of confidence in ITT's restructuring plan, top executives of the New York-based company vowed to retain their ITT shares.
Prodded by an investor during a conference call, Araskog said he did not intend to tender his shares in the company's $2.1 billion stock buyback.
"It would be a strong vote of confidence in the stock if you were to say now that you do not plan on tendering," said the investor.
Araskog responded, "Then you've got a strong vote of confidence in the stock."
ITT also announced plans to sell a 32.9 percent stake in the telephone directories company to the New York investment firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice Inc. for $225 million in cash.

ITT said it recently bought the 20 percent of World Directories it did not own from BellSouth Corp. for $254 million in cash. Following the transaction with Clayton Dubilier, World Directories will have $1.05 billion in debt, giving it an initial total value of $1.7 billion.
